newsitem.title: USA: N.Carolina film studio now in bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: N.Carolina film studio now in bankruptcy.

text.p: Magder Studios, a movie studio founded by veteran Canadian filmmaker Zale Magder, has sought protection under the federal bankruptcy laws less than one year after being founded, the Raleigh News and Observer reported on Monday.
Studio executives said in the Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing that they need to pay off some $2 million in debts.
Since it opened in April, the studio filmed nine commercials and one feature-length movie, "Last Lives," starring Judge Reinhold.

Gary Magder, son of the studio's founder, said he believed the studio would be able to reopen this year. "I have spent a lot of time in California, and there's a lot of interest in North Carolina," he told the newspaper. "It's a viable place to shoot movies."
Magder Studios purchased 315 acres in downtown Yanceyville, a quiet North Carolina town of just over 2,000 residents.

Another movie studio built by filmmaker Dino De Laurentis also went bankrupt and was turned over to Carolco Pictures Inc. After Carolco fell into bankruptcy proceedings, the studio was purchased by EUE/Screen Gems.
Last year, 52 movies were shot in the state, adding some $391 million to the North Carolina economy and creating some 40,000 jobs.
